clinician.final_diagnosis: Endometriosis of the right forearm (ectopic endometrial tissue in flexor pronator musculature)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old right-hand-dominant female with a 18-month history of an intermittently painful mass in the medial aspect of her right forearm presented to the Orthopedic Department. The mass demonstrated a characteristic cyclic pain pattern, becoming increasingly tender and firm in the days before menses and during menstruation. Physical examination revealed a small palpable tender mass in the right flexor pronator musculature. Radiographs of the right forearm on admission showed no acute osseous or soft tissue abnormality. Ultrasound imaging demonstrated a circumscribed, hypoechoic mass with internal Doppler flow. An ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy was performed but yielded nondiagnostic results. Subsequently, an open biopsy with frozen section was performed, which confirmed the diagnosis of endometriosis. The patient was then referred to Obstetrics/Gynecology for further evaluation and treatment discussion. Gynecologic examination did not reveal evidence of pelvic endometriosis, supporting the diagnosis of isolated extragonadal endometriosis in the forearm.
